mechanism_narrative: A surge in housing starts (HOUST) above 950K units, indicating strong demand, boosts consumer confidence, leading to increased spending and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5d returns in > 50% of instances when HOUST > 950K, or Rank IC < 0.02 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 0.25% signals an accommodative monetary policy, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days, as investors seek higher yields.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns when FEDFUNDS < 0.25% are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) falls below 5%, indicating a tight labor market, and payroll employment (PAYEMS) grows by more than 200K in a month, the combined effect predicts positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days, as a strong labor market boosts economic growth.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 40% of instances when both conditions are met, or Rank IC < 0.01 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) above its 6-month moving average, signaling a supply-side recovery, leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days, as manufacturers' growth prospects improve.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.02 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns when INDPRO > 6-month MA are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in the GDP annual growth rate (GDPC1) below 2%, indicating sluggish demand, predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days, as investors reassess growth prospects.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 50% of instances when GDPC1 annual growth < 2%, or Rank IC < 0.01 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: The federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) increasing by more than 50 basis points in a quarter, signaling a monetary tightening cycle, predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days, as higher borrowing costs reduce demand.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 40% of instances when FEDFUNDS increases > 50bps, or Rank IC < 0.02 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) rises above 6% and payroll employment (PAYEMS) growth slows to less than 100K in a month, the combined effect predicts negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days, as a weakening labor market signals economic slowdown.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 30% of instances when both conditions are met, or Rank IC < 0.01 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Retail and food services sales (RSAFS) growing by more than 5% year-over-year, indicating strong consumer demand, always predicts positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days, as investors react to robust consumption data.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 5-day forward returns when RSAFS growth > 5% YoY are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).
